vocabulary.name: Swindlers & Grifters
vocabulary.definition: An individual con artist deceived specific victims -- customers, clients, elderly marks, or romantic partners -- for personal profit, without running a pooled investment fund, a company, or a religious front.

vocabulary.name: Unsafe Products & Corporate Cover-Ups
vocabulary.definition: A company knowingly sold, shipped, or kept operating a product, ride, or drug it knew was dangerous or contaminated, and hid that risk from the public to protect profit; excludes workplace-only accidents where no consumer product was sold.

vocabulary.name: Ponzi Schemes & Investment Fraud
vocabulary.definition: An operator ran a pooled-money fund, charity, or 'business' that paid old investors with new money or simply stole client/investor funds; excludes a lone employee quietly skimming from their own employer, which belongs under embezzlement.

vocabulary.name: Industrial & Environmental Disasters
vocabulary.definition: Negligence, cost-cutting, or ignored warnings by a company or government caused a mass-casualty accident, toxic contamination, or environmental poisoning; covers plant/mine/rig disasters and pollution, not a packaged product sold to consumers.

vocabulary.name: Fabricated Stories & Hoaxes for Fame
vocabulary.definition: Someone invented or staged a dramatic personal story, illness, tragedy, or event mainly to win sympathy, media attention, or an entertainment opportunity, rather than to run an ongoing money-extraction scheme.

vocabulary.name: Identity Fraud & Impostors
vocabulary.definition: Someone assumed a false identity, faked credentials, or faked their own death or disappearance to gain access, escape consequences, or start a new life; excludes a spiritual/ministry persona used to extract money, which belongs under religious cons.

vocabulary.name: Political & Official Corruption
vocabulary.definition: An elected or appointed public official abused their office for personal gain, took bribes, or ran a cover-up from within government; excludes private-sector fraud with no public office involved.

vocabulary.name: When Exposure Turns Violent
vocabulary.definition: A fraud, grievance, or impending exposure escalated directly into murder, family annihilation, or an armed standoff, where the violence is the consequence of the cover-up unraveling.

vocabulary.name: Corporate Exploitation of People & Animals
vocabulary.definition: A business's underlying model depended on exploiting vulnerable workers, captive animals, or a captive audience, prioritizing profit over their welfare, apart from any single unsafe product it sold.

vocabulary.name: Embezzlement & Insider Theft
vocabulary.definition: A trusted employee, officer, or fiduciary secretly stole from the organization or person they served over time using their own position of access, rather than pitching outside investors on a fund.

vocabulary.name: Government Cover-Ups
vocabulary.definition: A government body or public institution concealed a known danger, contamination, or misconduct from the citizens it was supposed to protect, as distinct from a private company hiding a defect in something it sold.

vocabulary.name: Rigged Games & Insider Cheating
vocabulary.definition: Someone with inside access to a contest, lottery, game show, or officiated sport secretly manipulated the outcome for personal financial gain.

vocabulary.name: Charismatic & Religious Cons
vocabulary.definition: A leader used a spiritual, prophetic, psychic, or ministry persona and followers' devotion to extract money or control; distinct from secular grifters who invoke no faith or spiritual authority.

vocabulary.name: Medical Harm & Exploiting the Dead
vocabulary.definition: A person exploiting a role of medical or funerary trust harmed living patients through fraudulent or unnecessary treatment, or desecrated and sold the bodies of the dead for profit.
